XIII. Dubium Secundum est, An ad Legis Obliga-
tionem requiratur populi consensus? Ex jam dictis
enim possit fortassis aliquis existimare potestatem
ferendi Leges ad Principem ita pleno jure pertinere,
ut ex nostrå sententia subditorum nullæ essent
omninò hac in re partes, nec, siquid ille statue-
rit, populo quicquam superesse, aliud quàm jussa
capessere & colla jugo subdere. Et sanè vide-
tur pro dominantium libidine, illud, Sic volo sic
jubeo, apud prisci sæculi Reges ita obtinuisse, dum
mera Principum arbitria pro Legibus erant: ut ip-
sum Tyranni nomen innocens initio honestum,
ex tam salutaris potentiæ fœdo abusu, in contu-
meliam jamdiu abierit, & horrendum aliquid auri-
bus nostris, quoties auditur, inferre putetur. At-
qui populi saltem consensum aliquem requiri, & ante
prænmonui; & ab omnibus, quos mihi videre con-
tigit, probatissimis scriptoribus conceditur. Adeò
ut ipsi Jesuitæ, qui sunt Oecumenicæ & nullis con-
clusæ finibus Pontificis sui Omnipotentiæ assertores
acerrimi, excusandos tamen ob non servatas Con-
cilii Tridentini & Bullæ Cœnæ Leges, eo solo no-
mine putent in Germaniâ & alibi multos, quòd in
iis gentibus nunquam fuerint illæ Leges usu receptæ.
Dico igitur, & est communis sententia, institutas
& propositas à capite communitatis seu Principe
Leges ; non obligare subditos, nec vim Legis
habere, nisi ab ipsa communitate recipiantur, &
utentium vel suffragiis vel moribus comprobentur.

page.notes: The printed word after "prænmonui" reads "præmonui" in the scan; the letters are doubtful in the print and are marked as read. The bottom line is cut off by the edge of this part. "Obliga-tionem" and "con-tigit" continue in the second part. The print has a few doubtful letters where the ink is faint, in particular "prænmonui", which is copied as printed and should be checked against the original. The left margin fragments are cut at the edge of the scan and their placement against the lines is approximate. Cut-off words at the top of the first line are not visible, so the paragraph is marked as a continuation. The Greek in the text and the catchword "sâ" are doubtful and not certain readings.
